name: La Aurora International Airport
before:
Guatemala City's airport, and fourth busiest in Central America behind Panama, Costa Rica and El Salvador. It is only 6.4 km south of the centre and 25 km from Antigua Guatemala, which is where most leisure clients are actually heading, so the transfer is genuinely short.

The one long haul link worth knowing is Madrid. Iberia has flown non-stop with A340s since October 2004, a route opened when the airline closed its Miami hub and stopped routing passengers through it.

There is a single runway of 2,987 metres, and two VIP lounges: Los Añejos Business Lounge and the Copa Club, the latter for Copa Airlines and United passengers.

The airport is run directly by Guatemala's General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics, whose head office is on the site in Zone 13.
after:
Guatemala City's airport sits 6.4 km south of the city centre and about 22 km in a straight line from Antigua Guatemala. It handled more than five million passengers in 2025.

Flights between Madrid and Guatemala City carried 95,563 passengers in 2024, the latest year Eurostat has published for the route.

There is a single runway of 2,987 metres, and the airport is run by Guatemala's civil aviation directorate, the DGAC.

claims.note: start.mjs found no archived copy of the article the Overview was drafted from, so wikipedia-now (revision of 2026-08-26) is source 1 throughout this ledger.

claims.note: The coordinates check puts the airport 6.6 km from the GeoNames centre of Guatemala City at 193 degrees, south, so the stated 6.4 km and the bearing pass. start.mjs printed a CHECK line pairing '6.4 km south' with Antigua; that is the tool matching the wrong place, as the 6.4 km is from the city centre.

claims.claim: about 22 km in a straight line from Antigua Guatemala
claims.inAfter: about 22 km in a straight line from Antigua Guatemala
claims.note: Was '25 km from Antigua Guatemala'. Two independent position sets agree on about 22 km in a straight line (22.3 km from OurAirports and GeoNames, 22.4 km from Wikipedia's own coordinates). The 25 km passes the coordinates check, but no source says whether it is a road distance, and none gives the road distance or journey time, so the straight line is given and named as such.

Straight-line distance from Antigua Guatemala to La Aurora International Airport, from the Wikipedia coordinates: 22.4 km, bearing 83 degrees, which is east

claims.claim: more than five million passengers in 2025
claims.inAfter: It handled more than five million passengers in 2025.
claims.note: Replaces 'fourth busiest in Central America behind Panama, Costa Rica and El Salvador' (cut below), the same measure made current. Prensa Libre (26 January 2026), from DGAC data: more than 5.1 million in 2025 (2,573,651 arrivals and 2,555,884 departures), up from 2024. La Hora (23 July 2026) quotes the vice-minister of transport, Fernando Suriano: 'we have more than five million passengers', the current yearly level, which bears the 2025 figure out. His 'growing at more than 10 per cent' is not used: the DGAC figures Prensa Libre gives show about 4 per cent for 2025. Wikipedia's infobox gives 4,919,850 for 2024.

claims.inAfter: Flights between Madrid and Guatemala City carried 95,563 passengers in 2024, the latest year Eurostat has published for the route.
claims.note: Replaces 'The one long haul link worth knowing is Madrid. Iberia has flown non-stop with A340s since October 2004...' (cut below) with the one dated fact about the route that could be read: Eurostat's count of passengers carried between Madrid-Barajas and La Aurora, which has figures for 2010, 2012 to 2019 and 2023 to 2024, and none for 2011 or 2020 to 2022. No source from the last 12 months names the airline now flying it (Iberia's site refused the link lister with a 403; Prensa Libre's and La Hora's Iberia pages stop in 2022 and 2023), so no airline is named and the sentence is dated rather than put in the present tense. Wikipedia confirms the route itself.

claims.note: Was 'run directly by'. La Hora (26 August 2026): the culture ministry changed the heritage rules for La Aurora so that the DGAC can carry out maintenance, repair and modernisation work there itself. Wikipedia: administered by the DGAC. 'Directly' is dropped as neither source frames it that way.

claims.claim: fourth busiest in Central America behind Panama, Costa Rica and El Salvador
claims.wasBefore: and fourth busiest in Central America behind Panama, Costa Rica and El Salvador
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, with no figures or year. The 2025 figures read are consistent with El Salvador still being ahead (La Aurora more than 5.1 million, DGAC via Prensa Libre; El Salvador more than 5.2 million, CEPA's own release, see ledger/SAL.json), but Panama's and Costa Rica's current figures were not read, so the rank is not confirmed. Replaced by the passenger total (above).

sources.quote: The airport is the fourth-busiest in Central America in terms of passenger traffic behind Tocumen International Airport in Panamá, Juan Santamaría International Airport in Costa Rica, and the El Salvador International Airport.

claims.why: Made precise as the straight-line distance two position sets agree on (above).

claims.claim: most leisure clients are heading to Antigua, so the transfer is genuinely short
claims.wasBefore: which is where most leisure clients are actually heading, so the transfer is genuinely short.
claims.why: No source says where most leisure clients go, and none gives the road distance or time to Antigua (the 25 km is close to the 22 km straight line). The FCDO's warnings about the tourist routes out of Guatemala City are held back below.

claims.claim: the one long haul link worth knowing is Madrid
claims.wasBefore: The one long haul link worth knowing is Madrid.
claims.why: A judgement, and 'the one' could not be checked. The Madrid route is kept, dated (above). For the record, La Hora (31 July 2026) reports Air Canada keeping its Montreal to Guatemala City route open all year, and the DGAC noted a Boeing 787 on one of its flights in May 2026; whether that counts as long haul is a matter of definition (held back below).

claims.claim: Iberia non-stop with A340s since October 2004, after closing its Miami hub
claims.wasBefore: Iberia has flown non-stop with A340s since October 2004, a route opened when the airline closed its Miami hub and stopped routing passengers through it.
claims.why: The 2004 start and the Miami hub rest on Wikipedia alone: its source, Travel Weekly, answered with Cloudflare's 'Just a moment...' check (recorded, not retried). The A340s also rest on Wikipedia alone, and its wording ('introduced ... aboard Airbus A340s') describes the 2004 launch, not the aircraft flown now. 'Since 2004' is also broken by Eurostat's gap from 2020 to 2022. Prensa Libre (28 February 2022) shows Iberia flying Madrid to Guatemala City, going on to San Salvador, in 2022, but nothing from the last 12 months names the airline, and Iberia's own site refused the link lister (403), so it was not tried again.

claims.claim: two VIP lounges: Los Añejos Business Lounge and the Copa Club
claims.wasBefore: and two VIP lounges: Los Añejos Business Lounge and the Copa Club, the latter for Copa Airlines and United passengers.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and facilities change. Copa's site answered the link lister with a 401 (not retried), Wikipedia's Copa source is a 2011 page in the web archive (blocked), and the DGAC's portal builds its pages by script with no links to follow.

claims.claim: run directly; the DGAC's head office on the site in Zone 13
claims.wasBefore: The airport is run directly by Guatemala's General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics, whose head office is on the site in Zone 13.
claims.why: The DGAC's role is kept (above). The head office and Zone 13 rest on Wikipedia alone: the DGAC's portal (dgac.gob.gt) is a script-built app whose old statistics addresses now open its home page, and it offers no links to its contact pages.

claims.claim: FCDO: taxis, protests, robberies on tourist routes, volcanoes
claims.why: Held back: the FCDO says visitors can buy pre-paid taxi vouchers from the INGUAT tourist office in the arrivals terminal, that protesters may block roads and public facilities, including the international airport, without notice, that there have been armed attacks or robberies on most tourist routes between Guatemala City, Antigua, Tikal, Petén and Lake Atitlán, and that there is a risk of volcanic eruptions. Useful to a UK agent, but nothing in the old text to replace. For Andy to decide.

claims.claim: a new airport to replace much of La Aurora (phase zero)
claims.why: Held back: La Hora (23 July 2026) reports the vice-minister of transport saying the government has begun 'phase zero' of a new international airport that would, in the medium to long term, largely replace La Aurora because it is nearing capacity, with Masagua in Escuintla mentioned as a possible site. One source, and a plan rather than a change a traveller will meet now.

claims.claim: Air Canada flies Montreal to Guatemala City all year
claims.why: Held back: La Hora (31 July 2026) reports that Air Canada, which first landed here from Montreal on 3 October 2025, will keep the route open all year. One source, and the old text names no airline route other than Madrid.
